definitions.explanation: A small satellite campus operated by a main school ({本校|ほんこう}), typically set up in a remote area so that local children do not have to travel far. Many are tiny, with a handful of pupils and combined-grade classes.

examples.japanese: {島|しま}に{小|ちい}さな{分校|ぶんこう}がある。
examples.english: There is a small branch school on the island.

examples.japanese: この{分校|ぶんこう}の{生徒|せいと}は{五人|ごにん}だけだ。
examples.english: This branch school has only five pupils.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{数|かず}が{減|へ}ったため、{村|むら}の{分校|ぶんこう}は{来年|らいねん}{閉校|へいこう}することになった。
examples.english: Because the number of children has fallen, the village branch school is to close next year.

notes:
Composed of {分|ぶん} (divided, branch) + {校|こう} (school). Always defined against a {本校|ほんこう} (main campus), which handles administration and record-keeping.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {分校|ぶんこう}に{通|かよ}う: to attend a branch school
- {分校|ぶんこう}を{閉|と}じる: to close a branch school
- {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{分校|ぶんこう}: an elementary-school branch campus
- {分校|ぶんこう}から{本校|ほんこう}へ{移|うつ}る: to transfer from the branch to the main campus

CULTURAL NOTE:
Branch schools are strongly associated with mountain villages and small islands. As rural populations age and shrink, closures ({閉校|へいこう}) are frequent local news, and a closing {分校|ぶんこう} is a common shorthand in Japanese media for depopulation.
